data.text:
Ayala Malls has unveiled a fresh, minimalist look, and netizens are on the fence. 

On January 9, the mall developer’s official Facebook page revealed its new logo, with key malls gradually adopting the design. Some had already used the logo in company materials before the social media rollout. 

The redesign swaps the old brushstroke typeface for a singular ‘A’ symbol with clean sans serif text, reflecting a wider trend of companies opting for sleek, modern branding. Reactions have been mixed. 

Provincial malls like Ayala Center Cebu and Ayala Malls Abreeza in Davao received praise for retaining familiar elements from previous logos. However, others criticized the logo redesign for TriNoMa, which was symbolically represented by a triangle to harken its geographical status as the Triangular North of Manila. The new logo features a lowercase ‘T’ with circular elements. 

For Filipino shoppers and businesses, this shows how branding changes can influence customer perception and mall identity, affecting loyalty and foot traffic. 

Report by Kiara Gorrospe
